subject: Human Body
title: Delayed Soreness
description: A micro-lesson that makes Delayed Soreness usable.

hook.text: Work out hard and you feel fine. Two days later, getting out of bed hurts. Welcome to DOMS.

buildup.text: DOMS stands for delayed onset muscle soreness. It peaks 24 to 72 hours after unfamiliar exercise.

discovery.text: Eccentric movements cause the most damage: lowering a weight, walking downhill, or decelerating a sprint.

twist.text: Lactic acid doesn't cause DOMS. It clears within an hour of exercise. The soreness comes from micro-tears.

climax.text: DOMS is inflammation while muscles repair. It's annoying but signals adaptation. The next time hurts less.

punchline.text: Sore muscles aren't damaged. They're upgrading.
